items.title: Mississauga bylaw takes effect Sept. 1 to protect tenants, curb unlawful ‘renovictions’
items.summary: The bylaw introduces city-level oversight and financial safeguards alongside existing provincial eviction laws for tenants. Starting Sept. 1, landlords renovating rental units in Mississauga must obtain a municipal licence, help cover tenant relocation costs and provide regular work updates or face city fines. Mississauga is launching a new licensing framework to strengthen tenant protections and curb unlawful renovictions — evictions where landlords use renovation work as a reason to evict tenants and reset rents. From Sept. 1, under the Rental Repairs and Renovations Licensing Bylaw, landlords who issue a provincial N13 notice to vacate for major work must also apply for a city licence within seven days, according to a city press release. Renovations cannot begin until both the licence and a valid building permit are obtained. To qualify for the licence, property owners must prove that renovations require the unit to be vacant, have an active building permit and provide tenants with an official information package. Licensed landlords must also cover a one-time moving cost and make monthly top-up payments to tenants who temporarily relocate, and provide them with regular construction updates. According to the city, the bylaw was developed in consultations with tenants, property owners and community groups. Landlords who fail to comply will face municipal fines and enforcement penalties. The bylaw will work alongside provincial legislation while the Landlord and Tenant Board will have authority over eviction orders and tenancy disputes.

items.title: Mississauga teen's GPS tracker project emerges after Calgary tragedy, aiming to protect neurodivergent children
items.summary: Canada has no federal or provincial database tracking elopement incidents and no emergency alert equivalent to the Amber Alert for vulnerable individuals at high risk of wandering. Ashwin Chunchu, 17, is a Mississauga high school graduate who has developed StepSafe Kids, an affordable GPS tracker for neurodivergent individuals. The product is expected to launch in February 2027. When Ashwin Chunchu was seven, he used to slip away from his parents — drawn to a park or a street — and did not always know his way back. “That fear exists in a lot of children,” said Chunchu, now 17 and a recent Mississauga high school graduate. ” To support neurodivergent children and their families, Chunchu began building StepSafe Kids in March — a GPS tracker for neurodivergent children who wander — and launched a Kickstarter campaign that has already surpassed its funding goal ahead of its Sept. 3 end date. 99 or $349 as a one-time payment with no recurring fees, available to the first 200 supporters. As Chunchu works to bring this device to market, the death of 11-year-old Parker Wells, has reignited national debate about elopement risks, gaps in data, emergency alerting and public funding that leaves families of autistic individuals to manage that risk alone. Pictured here is a prototype of StepSafe Kids, a GPS Tracker for neurodivergent children, at risk of wandering or eloping. It’s expected to launch February 2027 and can be used as a clip on or attached to a lanyard for children with sensory sensitivities.

items.title: Police Believe a Now-Closed Mississauga Truck Stop Holds Clues in 20-Year-Old Cold Case
items.summary: According to INsauga, Wellington County OPP believe a now-closed Mississauga truck stop and a trucker connected to it could hold clues to a suspicious death that has gone unsolved for nearly two decades. INsauga reports the victim, a British Columbia woman identified as Penner, travelled to Ontario in February 2005, and her remains were discovered that August in a wooded picnic and rest area on Highway 7 between Rockwood and Guelph. It took investigators nearly 20 years to identify her, according to INsauga, even though Wellington County OPP have been working the case for almost 21 years. Police said Thursday they now have more specific information about Penner's movements around Ontario in the months before her death, including that she turned up at the Midland Mall in Midland, roughly 190 kilometres north of Rockwood, on June 30, 2005. INsauga notes the Rockwood Knights of Columbus created a memorial in Penner's honour, and investigators are renewing their appeal to the public for information about her last known whereabouts and who she may have been with.

items.title: Now in Its 15th Year, Mississauga Italfest Returns to Celebration Square This Weekend
items.summary: According to INsauga, Mississauga Italfest returns to Celebration Square this weekend for its 15th year, with organizers expecting large crowds over two days of Italian food, music and entertainment. INsauga reports the free festival runs Friday and Saturday and has grown from a small local celebration founded in 2012 by a group of Canadian Italians into one of Ontario's Top 100 Festivals, drawing visitors from across the province, Canada, the United States and even Italy. Attendees can expect authentic Italian food, fresh pasta and pizza, espresso and cannoli from food trucks and more than 60 artisan vendors, according to INsauga. Music and entertainment will take over the Celebration Square stages throughout the weekend, INsauga reports, featuring international performers, Italian folk acts, heritage dancers, regional choirs and Canadian music veteran Alfie Zappacosta. The outlet notes the festival has become a major fixture on Mississauga's summer calendar since it was founded in 2012.

items.title: Mississauga's Santa Claus Parade Returns Nov. 21 With Call for Floats Now Open
items.summary: According to INsauga, the City of Mississauga is now organizing this year's Santa Claus parade, set for Saturday, November 21 in the downtown core, after what officials called a highly successful return of the parade to City Centre near Square One last year following a nearly 25-year absence. INsauga reports the city is putting out a call for float entries and walking groups to take part in what it hopes will become a signature winter experience for years to come. This year's parade carries the theme Sauga's Home for the Holidays, meant to showcase the traditions, cultures, stories and people that make the city feel like home, according to the city. The lighting of the Christmas tree at Celebration Square and the seasonal opening of Mississauga's largest outdoor ice rink, also at the square, are scheduled for the same afternoon and evening as the parade, INsauga notes. City officials say interested organizations should apply early, since applications will be reviewed on a first-come, first-served basis and close September 30 or once the parade reaches capacity.

items.title: Regional Chair Iannicca Leads Push for Infrastructure and Housing Funding at Ontario Municipal Conference
items.summary: According to INsauga, Peel Region officials used this week's Association of Municipalities of Ontario conference to press the provincial government for more support on infrastructure, housing, healthcare and other essential services as Mississauga, Brampton and Caledon continue to grow. INsauga reports Regional Chair Nando Iannicca, along with members of regional council and senior staff, met with provincial ministers, parliamentary assistants and ministry officials to discuss the region's priorities. One of the region's top priorities, according to INsauga, was securing long-term infrastructure funding to keep pace with growth and offset pressures tied to development charges. In a meeting with the Ministry of Infrastructure, Peel officials pushed for provincial funding to support growth-related projects and the infrastructure needed for new housing and economic development, and INsauga reports the province and Peel committed to continuing that work together. Housing was another major focus of the region's discussions, this time with the Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing, where officials raised housing affordability, homelessness and the need to expand the supply of affordable housing while strengthening the municipal-provincial partnership, according to INsauga.

items.title: Twin 16-Storey Towers Now Proposed for Dundas Street Plaza Redevelopment, Down From 18 Storeys
items.summary: According to INsauga, a proposal to redevelop a plaza at 1225 Dundas Street East, just west of Dixie Road, has been revised again as it heads back for review next month. INsauga reports the site currently houses several businesses, including Danforth Food Market, Baituna Furniture and Spoon and Fork. The project has changed shape more than once since developers first applied in 2022 for a 12-storey apartment building with 462 units, ground-floor retail and 34 townhouses. By 2024, according to INsauga, the plan had grown to an 18-storey terraced building with two point towers connected by a shared nine-storey podium. The latest version submitted to the City of Mississauga scales that back to two 16-storey apartment buildings connected by a six-storey podium, INsauga reports, with developers Stephen-Mitchell Reality Limited, Whitehorn Investments Limited, Lynrob Investments Limited, Richco Investments Limited and Tobdele Investments Limited behind the application.

items.title: 1930 Meadowvale Village Bridge Gets Restoration Work as Wider Road Study Continues
items.summary: According to INsauga, Peel Region has closed one lane of the Old Derry Road bridge in Mississauga's Meadowvale Village area from today through Friday to allow restoration work on the structure. INsauga reports the bridge crosses the Credit River between Historic Trail and Credit Valley Conservation Road, with traffic control measures in place in the area for the next three days. The bridge, built in 1930, is a designated heritage structure within the Meadowvale Village Heritage Conservation District and serves as a scenic gateway into the historic community, according to INsauga. The restoration work comes as the City of Mississauga carries out a broader environmental assessment study for Old Derry Road, launched earlier this year, INsauga notes. That study is considering improvements including pavement rehabilitation, new cycling infrastructure and the repair or replacement of existing bridge structures along the road, including the Old Derry Road bridge itself.

items.title: Crombie Pledges Outside Audit of City Budget as She Seeks Return to Mayor's Office
items.summary: According to The Pointer, former Mississauga mayor Bonnie Crombie says that if voters return her to the office she held for nearly a decade, she plans to bring in an outside auditor to review every line of the city's budget. The Pointer reports Crombie is entering what is shaping up to be the most contentious mayoral race Mississauga has seen in decades, and that her early campaign messaging is built around the idea of using taxpayer dollars effectively without resorting to cuts that would hurt residents later. In the wide-ranging interview, according to The Pointer, Crombie argued there is room to find real savings for taxpayers without abandoning investment in the city's future. The outlet notes her platform comes against a backdrop of a growing infrastructure gap, large proposed downtown growth projects and a rising police budget that Peel politicians have largely avoided challenging. The Pointer reports Crombie has said that finding this balance, between what the city actually needs from taxpayers and the more politically popular route of promising unrealistic cuts, will be central to her campaign.
